title: Go
blurb: Goroutines, channels, generics, iterators, stdlib HTTP/JSON and production Go (1.24–1.27).

quiz.question: What does `go vet` plus `go fix` (1.26+) give you?
options: Suspicious-construct analysis plus push-button modernizers for new idioms
quiz.explanation: vet finds bugs (printf mismatches, copying locks); go fix now hosts modernizers that rewrite code to current idioms.

quiz.question: An unbuffered channel send (`ch <- v`)…
options: Blocks until a receiver takes the value
Drops the value if nobody listens
quiz.explanation: Unbuffered = synchronous handoff. Buffered (cap n) blocks only when full.

quiz.question: Which fixes a data race on a shared counter?
quiz.explanation: Sleep/GOMAXPROCS hide races; mutexes, atomics, or 'share by communicating' fix them. Verify with -race.

quiz.question: `iter.Seq[T]` (range-over-func, Go 1.23+) lets you…
options: Write `for v := range myIterator` over a custom yield function
quiz.explanation: A Seq is func(yield func(T) bool); range calls it, and yield returning false stops early.

quiz.question: `json:"when,omitzero"` (Go 1.24) differs from omitempty by…
options: Calling IsZero() when available, else comparing to the zero value
quiz.explanation: omitzero respects IsZero (e.g. time.Time.IsZero); omitempty uses a fixed emptiness table.

quiz.question: `new(expr)` in Go 1.26…
options: Returns a pointer to a new variable initialized with expr's value
quiz.explanation: new(x) replaces ptr-helper functions: *T pointing at a copy of x.

quiz.question: A nil interface holding a typed nil pointer (`var e error = (*MyErr)(nil)`)…
options: Is non-nil (it has a type descriptor), a classic gotcha
quiz.explanation: Interfaces are (type, value); typed-nil has a type, so e != nil. Return nil explicitly.

quiz.question: Context cancellation should be used for…
options: Passing optional params to any function
Deadlines/cancellation/scoped values across a request's call graph
quiz.explanation: ctx is request-scoped: cancel on client disconnect/timeout; don't store it in structs or use for optional params.

problems.title: Fix the goroutine leak
problems.prompt: A handler starts `go poll()` per request and poll loops forever on time.Tick. What's wrong and what's the minimal fix?
problems.solution: Each request leaks a goroutine + ticker forever. Fix: pass the request context, select on ctx.Done(), and time.NewTicker with defer ticker.Stop().

problems.title: Bounded worker pool
problems.prompt: Fetch 10k URLs with at most 32 concurrent requests, collecting errors. Sketch the design.
problems.solution: Jobs channel + N workers, or errgroup.Group with SetLimit(32); one result slot per index; context timeout; close response bodies; aggregate errors.

problems.title: Generic filter with iterators
problems.prompt: Write Where[T](seq iter.Seq[T], keep func(T) bool) iter.Seq[T] using range-over-func.
problems.solution: return func(yield func(T) bool) { for v := range seq { if keep(v) && !yield(v) { return } } }

problems.title: Graceful shutdown
problems.prompt: An HTTP server must drain in-flight requests on SIGTERM within 30s, then exit non-zero if it can't. Outline the code.
problems.solution: signal.NotifyContext for SIGTERM; run server in goroutine; on ctx done, Shutdown with 30s timeout context; log forced-close and os.Exit(1) on timeout; wait for background workers via WaitGroup.
